What is the reference period or as-of date on participation rate in Alberta, 2026-07 (seasonally adjusted)?
response_text:
**REF_DATE = `2026-07` — July 2026.** That's the only temporal field in the file; the participation rate row (vector `v2064517`, coordinate `10.8.1.1.1.1`) carries 69.2% with a standard error of 0.5 (`v101889152`) at that date.

Two things worth flagging about how to read that as-of date:

- **It's a month-level label, not an instant.** In the Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey (Table 14-10-0287, from which these vectors come), the actual reference period is the week containing the 15th of the month — so July 2026 data describes labour market status during the week of July 12–18, 2026. The CSV does not carry that detail; you'd have to attach it from the LFS documentation.
- **"Seasonally adjusted" means the value is not a raw July observation.** Seasonal adjustment is estimated over the full series history, so a seasonally adjusted July 2026 figure is subject to revision when the series is re-adjusted, and it isn't directly comparable to an unadjusted July reading.

If you need a single as-of timestamp for a database field, `2026-07-01` (period start) or `2026-07` as a year-month is the honest encoding; anything more precise would be inventing precision the file doesn't have. The vintage of the file itself (when StatCan released this estimate) is not present in the data at all — no release-date or revision column — so if provenance matters downstream, that has to be captured separately at ingest.
